stream: record {0x00040008, data_off or 2, code_off, 0, 0, 0, 0x40000000} running the binding DMA program (f0040000 f4060100 d3000000) on data whose src0/src1 point at a mapped 16-byte entry; then 0x80000000
proves: the CDM fetches a record, the PDS runs from the heap at the expected base, DMA into the common store works
failure signatures: a bank-0 fault at heap base + code_off means the PDS base is not where the heap is mapped (fix the base); a fault at the entry address means the DMA source; a stall with no fault means the record format

stream: as J2a with src0 at an unmapped VA (e.g. 0x7_00000000)
proves: a bank-0 fault at exactly that VA proves the PDS program executed
USC dispatch and the USC code base
failure signatures: a bank-0 fault at heap base + 0x40 means the USC base differs from the PDS base (map the kernel at the USC-base heap)

stream: record 0 = the binding DMA (t1), record 1 = {0x00002106, store PDS data offset, store PDS code offset, 0, 0, 0, 0x40000000}, then 0x80000000; argument entry {output VA, 0x00010001}; the store kernel from Orchard's G9P compiler (Mesa, A9 mode with apple_g4p) storing 0xcafe0001
read: the output word (after an SLC flush if cached), stamps
failure signatures: the output still at its sentinel with stamps 1 = the kernel ran but stored elsewhere (check its buffer index and offset); a fault at the output VA = a mapping or flag problem

boot: add an end-of-pass barrier: Metal's A8 stream has three more records after the kernel (40008 1488a 14800, 4 1418a 14100, 7 14214 14200); on the A10 Orchard found that without the end-of-pass records the last workgroups are lost and the GPU can wedge. Their A8 programs are not published
